verdict.rationale: The relay connects arbitrary publishers to subscribers and fans out at scale. A production report describes new independent consumers (archiver, live transcription, voice ID) subscribing to one published Opus broadcast without any change to the publisher, so adding a subscriber is well supported. Selecting a single track out of a multi-track broadcast is only implied by the custom-track and 'send only when someone is watching' claims, not explicitly documented. Missing for 10: explicit first-party docs on per-track subscription within a broadcast, a documented agent/headless subscriber example (e.g. via Python bindings), and caveats such as the relay not preserving packet timing and the race on late subscription.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent subscribes to a single track of a live broadcast without the publisher changing anything about how it publishes

citations.quote: publish Opus to one relay, which fans out to independent subscribers: an S3 archiver, Zoom Scribe Live transcription, and voice ID. They say adding a new consumer no longer requires another recorder or a migration.
A server connecting publishers to subscribers
Dynamic announcements, connecting arbitrary publishers to subscribers.
